projects.description:
In 2025, the Joint UN Team on AIDS (JUTA) supported Ghana to strengthen governance, coordination and financial sustainability mechanisms of the national HIV response, ensuring stronger oversight and strategic alignment with global commitments under the Global AIDS Strategy.

UN partners provided technical and programmatic support to national institutions, including the Ghana AIDS Commission, Ministry of Health, National AIDS Control Programme, and the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), to enhance planning, programme review and coordination processes across the HIV response. These efforts contributed to strengthening institutional capacity to manage complex partnerships and financing streams supporting HIV programmes.

Support from the UN system also contributed to improving strategic engagement with major financing mechanisms, particularly the Global Fund and PEPFAR, helping national stakeholders align programmatic priorities with available resources while reinforcing accountability mechanisms. Technical support facilitated coordination among key partners and strengthened national oversight of programme implementation and performance monitoring.

In addition, UN partners supported national processes related to resource mobilization, financial analysis and programme planning, helping to ensure sustainability of HIV programmes and reinforcing national readiness for the development of future Global Fund investments. These efforts contributed to supporting the effective implementation of the HIV components of the Global Fund NFM3 grant, while strengthening national capacity to design and position innovative HIV interventions within the upcoming Global Fund NFM4 funding cycle.

Collectively, these interventions strengthened governance and coordination of the HIV response in Ghana while supporting national leadership to mobilize and strategically allocate resources needed to sustain progress towards epidemic control.

projects.name: Enhanced capacity for coordination, oversight, and innovation in HIV combination prevention, eMTCT/Triple Elimination, DSD, Integrated services  treatment, care and support services focused on key and vulnerable populations is sustained to ensure progress towards the 95-95-95 cascade, reduction of new infections and AIDS related deaths in Ghana.
projects.description:
In 2025, the Joint UN Team on AIDS (JUTA) supported national efforts to strengthen coordination, oversight and innovation across the HIV prevention and treatment continuum to accelerate progress towards the 95-95-95 targets and the reduction of new infections and AIDS-related deaths in Ghana.

Through technical assistance and strategic collaboration with the Ministry of Health, Ghana Health Service, the National AIDS Control Programme, and the Ghana AIDS Commission, UN agencies strengthened national capacity to plan, coordinate and deliver integrated HIV services, particularly for key and vulnerable populations.

UN support contributed to strengthening governance and programmatic oversight of HIV prevention and treatment programmes, including improved coordination mechanisms across national institutions responsible for prevention, treatment and community programming. This helped reinforce alignment between national strategies and implementation frameworks supporting combination prevention, differentiated service delivery (DSD), and the integration of HIV services within broader health systems.

Targeted support also enhanced national capacity to advance elimination of mother-to-child transmission (eMTCT) and Triple Elimination initiatives, including strengthening programme monitoring, data use and service delivery innovations that improve access to testing, treatment and follow-up care for pregnant women and infants.

At the service delivery level, UN partners supported innovations in differentiated service delivery and integrated treatment and care models, helping health facilities and community systems expand people-centred approaches to HIV testing, treatment adherence and long-term care. These efforts were complemented by community-based interventions that strengthened engagement of civil society and community networks working with key populations, helping to improve service uptake and continuity of care.

Collectively, these efforts contributed to strengthening national systems for coordination and programme oversight while supporting innovative approaches to HIV prevention and treatment delivery, reinforcing Ghana’s progress towards achieving the 95-95-95 cascade and sustaining gains in reducing HIV infections and AIDS-related mortality.

projects.name: Ghana NAP. Enhancing multi-sector planning and capacity for effective adaptation in Ghana FSP
projects.description:
This project will develop a NAP adaptation process that will produce a costed adaptation strategy for the country and provide the tools, mechanisms, system and information with which to replicate the NAP process at regular intervals and to mainstream the adaptation strategy into sector and District development plans.
Expected outcomes from this project are as follows:
• Central level systems and Processes for the development of the NAP developed and mainstreamed at all level
• District level systems and processes for the development of the NAP;
• Enabling environment to promote private sector investment in adaptation strength-ened.
• Learning about the NAP process disseminated
The project builds on a baseline which includes extensive stakeholder consultations to develop a climate change policy, a green growth strategy, a national climate change strategy, a climate change masterplan and some limited work to develop adaptation capacities in 10 Districts (out of a total of 264 Districts). Capacity needs in relation to adaptation planning have been consistently stated throughout all these documents to be in the areas of developing systems for evidence-based decision-making. This NAP proposal focuses on this at the national and District level as well as raising awareness among planners, politicians and the private sector, building capacities for NAP planning, strengthening linkages between Districts and national level planning and strategies to raise the level of political leadership on adaptation. The project will strengthen adaptation planning capacity in 10 Districts.

projects.name: Transnational coastal development strategy developed for Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire for improved transboundary governance system and cooperation for sharing best practices and cross-fertilization of ideas for enhancing adaptation in coastal communities.
projects.description:
The development of a Transnational Coastal Development Strategy will take into account the necessity to 
better manage and preserve natural ecosystems as infrastructures for climate adaptation. Through the Transnational Coastal Development Strategy, ecosystems located in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, as well as along the border will be managed to preserve and/or enhance their adaptive capacities. Transnational Coastal Development 
Strategy will also improve ecological connectivity in the region. 
Additionally, the development of the Transnational Coastal Development Strategy will lead to improved understanding of spatial planning strategies for climate adaptation in the neighboring country and reinforced knowledge sharing in between the two countries on good practices for climate adaptation.
Also, the Transnational Coastal Development Strategy will allow to reduce economic losses and damage from climate-related disasters and from their possible consequences on transboundary migration.

projects.name: Capacities of national authorities, communities and other key stakeholders strengthened, stigma and discrimination among KVP are reduced and the protection and promotion of human rights among all target groups are upheld through strategic partnerships and technical assistance to mitigate the risk an dimpact of HIV on those furthest behind in line with the 10-10-10 targets
projects.description:
In 2025, the Joint UN Team on AIDS (JUTA) supported Ghana in strengthening national and community capacities to address HIV-related stigma, discrimination and human rights barriers affecting key and vulnerable populations, in line with the global 10-10-10 targets.

Through strategic partnerships with government institutions, civil society organisations and community networks, UN partners provided technical assistance to strengthen national frameworks and institutional capacities for protecting the rights of people living with HIV and key populations. Engagement with national authorities contributed to reinforcing governance and accountability mechanisms addressing stigma and discrimination within the HIV response, while promoting the integration of human rights approaches into national HIV programming.

At the community level, targeted initiatives strengthened the capacity of networks of people living with HIV and key population organisations to engage with institutions, monitor rights violations, and advocate for equitable access to health and social services. Community actors were supported to enhance peer outreach, awareness raising and referral mechanisms that enable affected populations to access services without fear of stigma or discrimination.

Technical assistance and partnership efforts also supported dialogue and collaboration between community organisations and public institutions, helping to foster trust and strengthen mechanisms for addressing discrimination and other structural barriers to HIV services. These initiatives contributed to improving the enabling environment for HIV prevention, treatment and care while reinforcing community leadership within the national response.

Collectively, these interventions contributed to advancing a rights-based HIV response in Ghana, strengthening institutional and community capacity to prevent and respond to stigma and discrimination, and supporting progress towards achieving the 10-10-10 targets.

projects.description:
This proposal seeks to support developing countries to prepare and submit their BTRs and NCs as outlined in the Enhanced Transparency Framework. It is expected that these reports will not only inform national prioritization and planning agenda related to climate change, but will also inform the global stock take to be undertaken in Yr. 2028. 

The objective of this project is to support forty-three (43) developing countries to prepare and submit BTRs and combined BTRs/NCs that comply with the UNFCCC/PA reporting requirements; and respond to their national development goals. The programme aims to support national governments fulfill essential communication requirements to the Convention and is in conformity with Objective 3 of the GEF-7 Climate Change Focal Area, which focuses on fostering enabling conditions for mainstreaming mitigation concerns into sustainable development strategies. The project will be implemented on an agreed full cost basis requiring only in-kind contribution by GEF-eligible countries, which will be communicated to UNEP during project implementation.

projects.name: National authorities and partners supported to improve HIV data quality assurance and utilization of data for policy decision making to improve the HIV response including HIV Estimates, GAM reporting, CLM and Operational Research.
projects.description:
In 2025, the Joint UN Team on AIDS (JUTA) supported national authorities and partners in Ghana to strengthen HIV data systems, improve data quality assurance, and enhance the use of strategic information for evidence-based decision making within the national HIV response.

Technical assistance provided by UN partners supported national institutions, including the Ghana AIDS Commission and the National AIDS Control Programme, to strengthen processes for data collection, analysis and validation across key national reporting platforms. This included support for HIV estimates generation, Global AIDS Monitoring (GAM) reporting, and national data review processes, contributing to improved accuracy, consistency and completeness of national HIV data.

UN partners also supported efforts to strengthen the use of community-generated data, including through community-led monitoring (CLM) initiatives. These efforts helped bridge community perspectives with national policy discussions by generating insights on service access, quality of care, and barriers experienced by key and vulnerable populations.

In addition, support was provided for operational research and analytical processes that enable national stakeholders to better interpret programme data and translate evidence into policy and programmatic improvements. These initiatives strengthened national capacity to use data to identify gaps in the HIV response, guide strategic planning, and improve accountability.

Collectively, these interventions contributed to strengthening Ghana’s strategic information systems, improving the availability and use of high-quality data to inform policies and programmes aimed at accelerating progress towards national HIV targets.

projects.name: Delivering integrated solutions to reduce carbon and increase resilience in buildings – Global and multi-country
projects.description:
Changes in the buildings and construction sector are essential to address the three planetary crises in UNEP’s 2022-2025 Medium-Term Strategy and the Sustainable Development Goals notably SDG 13, SDG 12 and SDG 11. The sector is responsible for about 40 per cent of global energy-related CO2 emissions and a major consumer of natural resources. It is a key sector for national economies and global demand for buildings is on the rise particularly in emerging and developing economies. The building and construction
sector’s demand for natural resources accelerates climate change, and inefficient, unhealthy buildings negatively impact human health and wellbeing. 

The project builds on the Global Alliance for Buildings and Construction, a voluntary, international, multistakeholder partnership hosted by UNEP since its creation at COP21 in 2015. With the GlobalABC, UNEP is creating a common language and vision through transparency, inclusion and cooperation among buildings and construction stakeholders who share the aim of decarbonizing buildings. This project will sustain the GlobalABC as the nucleus of a growing, global movement. It will also strengthen UNEP’s support for
sustainable buildings and construction projects in countries, and allow for further dissemination of tools, approaches and best practices for decarbonizing buildings at the global, regional, national, and local levels.

The project will address three major challenges hampering the transformation towards a zero-emission, efficient, and resilient buildings and construction sector. First, the lack of collaboration and coordination between buildings and construction value chain stakeholders which leads to isolated projects. Then, the lack of ambitious national strategies and policies for the decarbonization of buildings, which in turn hampers both policy change and finance for decarbonizing buildings. Finally, the insufficient awareness, knowledge, technologies, capacities and skills in countries to decarbonize buildings along their lifecycles.

projects.name: Improve knowledge and skills of NACOC officers while encouraging an organizational culture that respects human rights and rule of law
projects.description:
In 2024, UNODC strengthened its partnership with the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) to enhance institutional capacity in drug enforcement, policy implementation, and cross-border cooperation. A series of capacity-building initiatives were delivered to equip NACOC officers with specialized skills in intelligence-led investigations, interdiction techniques, and human rights-based approaches to drug control. 
Key activities included specialized training sessions on counter-narcotics operations, digital investigation tools, and case management systems, aimed at improving NACOC’s ability to detect and disrupt drug trafficking networks. Additionally, UNODC facilitated workshops on international drug policy frameworks, enabling NACOC to align national strategies with global best practices. 
To promote interagency and cross-border coordination, UNODC supported NACOC’s participation in regional dialogues and knowledge-sharing initiatives, fostering collaboration with law enforcement agencies across West Africa. Furthermore, in partnership with NACOC, UNODC provided technical assistance in policy development and institutional reforms, reinforcing a governance structure that prioritizes transparency, accountability, and respect for human rights.
